notes: Every frame was visually inspected in-session for sharpness and correct content; talking-head and transition frames were rejected and re-shot. Two on-screen editor search-box overlays are intentionally kept because they highlight the exact keyword Dan is discussing (scrape_loop_prompt; image-loop).

frames.label: stakeholder-trifecta
frames.shows: The 'The Stakeholder Trifecta' title slide with three nodes: You, Your Agents, Your Team.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Anchors the mindset shift the whole lesson hangs on — you write prompts for three readers, most importantly your agents. The image students should hold in mind before any format is introduced.

frames.label: l1-all-tools-prompt
frames.shows: all_tools.md open in-editor: '# List All Tools' title + the one-paragraph high-level prompt. A complete Level-1 prompt.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The smallest possible reusable prompt — two sections, no ceremony. Proves Level 1 is a real, useful format and demystifies where you start when you first notice repeat work.

frames.label: l2-prime-workflow-report
frames.shows: prime.md: description metadata, # Prime, Purpose, ## Workflow (git ls-files; read README.md), ## Report. The minimal Level-2 workflow prompt.
frames.why_for_weak_student: First sight of the pillar Workflow section and the input→work→output shape in the simplest possible form. Small enough to fully read; the template every later level extends.

frames.label: quick-plan-collapsed-sections
frames.shows: quick-plan.md with sections collapsed to H2s: metadata (allowed-tools, argument-hint, model: claude-opus-4-1-20250805), # Quick Plan, purpose, then collapsed ## Variables / ## Instructions / ## Workflow / ## Report.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The 'collapse to see the Lego blocks' move made literal — a weak student sees a prompt as a stack of swappable sections, not a wall of text. Also shows a pinned course-era model id (a current-practice flag).

frames.label: l3-build-line17-control-flow
frames.shows: build.md in full: metadata (Read,Write,Bash), Variables (PATH_TO_PLAN: $ARGUMENTS), Workflow line 17 'If no PATH_TO_PLAN is provided, STOP immediately and ask the user', Report (git diff --stat).
frames.why_for_weak_student: Control flow you can point at: one line turns a workflow into an early-return guard. Also the Level-5 higher-order example (a plan is passed IN), so it does double duty.

frames.label: l3-create-image-loop
frames.shows: create_image.md Workflow expanded: prerequisite STOP conditionals (system-prompt/tool checks) and the full <image-loop> … </image-loop> XML block that repeats NUMBER_OF_IMAGES times.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Shows the OTHER half of control flow — a natural-language loop delimited by an XML block — so the student sees conditionals (build) and loops (create_image) as distinct, nameable capabilities inside one Workflow section.

frames.label: l4-load-ai-docs-scrapers
frames.shows: load_ai_docs.md with the file explorer on the left (.claude/agents, commands, hooks; ai_docs/*.md). The Workflow loops URLs and calls '@agent-docs-scraper' via a <scrape_loop_prompt> block.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Delegation made concrete: a primary agent fires sub-agents (doc scrapers) to do work in parallel. The visible directory tree also orients the student in the whole codebase.

frames.label: l4-background-append-system-prompt
frames.shows: background.md header: description ('Fires off a full Claude Code instance in the background'), argument-hint [prompt] [model] [report-file], allowed-tools incl. Task, model: claude-opus-4-1-20250805, # Background Claude Code, purpose, collapsed Variables/Instructions/Workflow.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The second delegation flavor — a primary agent that launches a whole background Claude Code instance (and, in its Workflow, appends to that agent's system prompt). Bridges Level 4 delegation to the system-vs-user-prompt discussion.

frames.label: l6-metaprompt-specified-format
frames.shows: t_metaprompt_workflow.md: # MetaPrompt, purpose ('create a new prompt in the Specified Format … WebFetch everything in the Documentation'), Variables (HIGH_LEVEL_PROMPT: $ARGUMENTS), collapsed ## Workflow / ## Documentation / ## Specified Format.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The prompt that builds prompts, seen whole: a Template (Specified Format) + a Documentation context map. Shows why Level 6 is peak-leverage. (On-screen purpose says 'Instructions'; Dan corrects it live to 'Workflow'.)

frames.label: l7-expert-expertise-section
frames.shows: cc_hook_expert_plan.md: # Claude Code Hook Expert Plan, purpose, collapsed Variables/Instructions, and the EXPANDED ## Expertise section (File Structure for Claude Code Hooks tree: settings.json, hooks/, context_bundle_builder.py, commands/experts/cc_hook_expert/).
frames.why_for_weak_student: Makes the abstract 'self-improving' idea tangible: the Expertise section is real, sizeable embedded knowledge — the thing a separate _improve prompt rewrites over time. The Level-7 payoff in one screen.

frames.label: final-tier-list
frames.shows: The completed 'AGENTIC PROMPT TIER LIST' 5x5 grid — axes Useful↔Useless (Y) and Beginner↔Expert (X), tiers D/C/B/A/S — with every section and format placed, plus the SECTIONS & FORMATS pool below.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The single most valuable image in the chapter: the entire mental model in one grid. A weak student can memorize this and instantly recall each section's usefulness/skill trade-off. This frame is the ground truth the tier_list in extract.json was reconciled against.

frames.label: readme-spine-system-vs-user
frames.shows: README.md open (outline collapsed): '# Agentic Prompt Engineering', 'The prompt is THE fundamental unit of engineering', '## The 7 Levels' (Level 1-7 collapsed), '## Agentic Prompt Sections', '## System Prompts vs User Prompts — The most important difference is scope and persistence.' Left explorer lists the full command set.
frames.why_for_weak_student: One frame that is both the table of contents (7 levels + sections) and the on-ramp to the closing system-vs-user concept. Lets a student see the whole lesson's structure — and the full slash-command inventory — at a glance.

suggested_designed_diagrams: A clean redraw of the tier-list grid (from t2740) as a crisp print figure with tier legend and each cell labeled — the chapter's centerpiece figure.
A 'seven levels staircase' diagram: each step adds one capability (workflow → control flow → delegate → higher-order → template → self-improving) with the one section it introduces.
An Input → Workflow → Output block diagram mapping Variables / Workflow / Report onto the three-step frame.
